newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli parliament gets second-round budget cuts.
newsitem.headline: Israeli parliament gets second-round budget cuts.

text.p: Israel's Treasury presented to parliament on Wednesday an amended budget that includes 1.13 billion shekels in additional cuts and more than 600 million shekels in new, non-tax income, a spokeswoman said.

In presenting the amended budget, the Treasury estimated that Israel's current account deficit would reach $5.4 billion this year, up from previous estimates of about $5.0 billion. In the first nine months, the deficit was $4.71 billion.
A Treasury source said the ministry expected the Arrangements Law, which includes legislation related to the budget, to go to its final vote December 24 and the budget itself a week later.

Parliament has until December 31 to approve the budget, or the 1996 budget stays in effect for another three months. If parliament fails to vote a new budget by March 31, new elections must be called.

The spending cuts, which total about 6.1 billion shekels, have met powerful opposition in parliament, and political analysts say there is a good chance the budget will not be approved by the end of the year.
